description_full: Laopu Gold Co., Ltd. designs, manufactures, and sells jewelry products in Mainland China, Hong Kong, and Macau. It offers handmade goldware, including pendants, bracelets, rings, earrings, jewelry for babies, and gem-set jewelry, as well as gold antiques and collectibles. The company also provides maintenance and repair services for jewelry products. It sells its products through stores and online. The company was founded in 2009 and is headquartered in Beijing, the People's Republic of China.

financial_summary: LAOPU GOLD CO LTD is a mid-cap consumer cyclical business with a $7.4B market cap on $4.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +170% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 38% against a 9% cost of capital — a 29-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 42%.
The company is burning through $1.0B of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
Accruals are elevated at +55.1% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.7× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 47× is fortress-like.

Net dilution runs at 7.9% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and within its sector the business captures 3.0× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 377 companies in the universe; the top four hold 26% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 50% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 67% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 75% and a beta of 0.98, it moves roughly with the market.

val: The stock trades 70% below its blended-model fair value of $14.10, a meaningful margin of safety.

prof: ROIC of 38% clears the cost of capital of 8.8% by 29pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.52).
